item.title: [BM] Anwar Periksa Kerja Sendiri — PM Yang Juga Menteri Kewangan Bentangkan Bajet Dan Dakwa Ia Hebat
item.description:
Said by: Opposition / Budget Analysts

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-10-10

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Bajet 2026 dibentangkan oleh Anwar Ibrahim — sebagai Menteri Kewangan — kepada parlimen, di mana beliau duduk sebagai Perdana Menteri. Beliau kemudian mempertahankan bajetnya sendiri di parlimen, memuji pencapaiannya, dan menolak kritikan. Orang yang menulis peperiksaan juga orang yang memberikan markah.

🔥 Kenapa Ia Penting

Dalam mana-mana demokrasi yang berfungsi, fungsi kewangan mempunyai pengawasan bebas daripada kepimpinan politik. Apabila satu orang mengawal kedua-dua agenda politik dan dompet negara, tiada semakan bermakna terhadap keputusan fiskal. Peruntukan bajet menjadi alat politik tanpa penelitian bebas. Peranan Parlimen sebagai badan pengawasan bajet terjejas apabila PM/MK mengawal kedua-dua eksekutif dan agenda fiskal.

item.title: [BM] Pekerja Ekonomi Gig Masih Tanpa Perlindungan — Penghantar Grab Dan Foodpanda Pertaruhkan Nyawa Untuk Gaji Kemiskinan

item.title: Anwar Marks His Own Homework — PM Who Is Also Finance Minister Presents Budget and Claims It's Great
item.description:
Said by: Opposition / Budget Analysts

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-10-10

📌 What Happened

Budget 2026 was presented by Anwar Ibrahim — as Finance Minister — to parliament, where he sits as Prime Minister. He then defended his own budget in parliament, praised its achievements, and dismissed criticism. The person who wrote the exam is also the person who grades it.

🔥 Why It Matters

In any functional democracy, the finance function has oversight independent from the political leadership. When one person controls both the political agenda and the national wallet, there is no meaningful check on fiscal decisions. Budget allocations become political tools without independent scrutiny. Parliament’s role as a budget oversight body is undermined when the PM/FM controls both the executive and the fiscal agenda.

The Facts

Fact: Using B40 median income as a benchmark, homes need to be priced below RM300,000 to be considered affordable. The government set this as the ceiling price.

item.title: [BM] Bajet Sukan Dipotong — Atlet Bergelut Sementara Kerajaan Belanja Berbilion Untuk GLC

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Apabila pembantu politik PM sendiri dituduh rasuah dalam urus niaga perlombongan dan agensi antirasuah membebaskan mereka tanpa penjelasan awam yang boleh dipercayai, kebebasan agensi tersebut dipersoalkan. Dakwaan Bloomberg — bahawa Anwar campur tangan secara langsung untuk menghentikan siasatan — adalah letupan besar. Jika benar, ia bermakna pejuang antirasuah menghalang siasatan antirasuah. Jika palsu, kerajaan tidak memberikan bukti untuk menyangkalnya.

item.title: Farhash Wafa Cleared by MACC Over Sabah Mining — Muda Slams 'Pleasing the PM'
item.description:

Date: 2025-09-09

📌 What Happened

MACC cleared Anwar’s former aide Farhash Wafa over the Sabah mining scandal, despite Bloomberg alleging Anwar ordered MACC not to investigate. Muda accused MACC chief Azam Baki of ’trying to survive by pleasing the PM.'

🔥 Why It Matters

When a PM’s own political aide is accused of corruption in a mining deal and the anti-corruption agency clears them without a credible public explanation, the agency’s independence is in question. Bloomberg’s allegation — that Anwar directly intervened to stop the investigation — is explosive. If true, it means the anti-corruption crusader is obstructing anti-corruption investigations. If false, the government has not provided evidence to refute it.

item.title: [BM] Keluarga T20 Kini Guna Hospital Kerajaan — Golongan Kaya Pun Tak Mampu Penjagaan Kesihatan Swasta
item.description:
Said by: Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations / The Star

Category: Health

Date: 2025-09-08

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Gabungan Persatuan-Persatuan Pengguna Malaysia (FOMCA) membunyikan penggera bahawa malah keluarga T20 (20% berpendapatan tertinggi) kini beralih ke hospital kerajaan kerana penjagaan kesihatan swasta menjadi terlalu mahal. Pengurus kanan FOMCA Saral James Maniam memanggilnya ‘bendera merah besar.’

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Apabila rakyat Malaysia terkaya mendapati penjagaan kesihatan swasta tidak mampu dibayar, keseluruhan model pembiayaan penjagaan kesihatan telah runtuh. Keluarga-keluarga ini membanjiri hospital kerajaan yang sudah terbeban, mewujudkan barisan lebih panjang dan hasil lebih buruk untuk pesakit B40 dan M40 yang tiada alternatif. Sistem ini mengalami gelung kemusnahan: kos swasta meningkat → T20 beralih ke awam → sistem awam terbeban → kualiti merosot → tiada siapa mendapat penjagaan memadai.

item.title: [BM] Sistem Penjagaan Kesihatan Malaysia: 'Bom Jangka' — 2.83% KDNK Sementara Negara Lain Belanja Dua Kali Ganda
item.description:
Said by: P4H Network / University of Malaya Working Paper / The Star

Category: Health

Date: 2025-09-08

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Pelbagai analisis bebas telah mengisytiharkan sistem penjagaan kesihatan Malaysia sebagai ‘bom jangka.’ Perbelanjaan kesihatan awam hanya pada 2.83% KDNK pada 2023, jauh di bawah paras yang disyorkan WHO dan rakan serantau. Nisbah doktor-pesakit 1:417 menyembunyikan krisis sebenar di sektor awam, yang mengendalikan 80% katil hospital dengan 54% doktor. Negara ini kekurangan 11,000 pakar. Doktor muda bekerja 84 jam seminggu.

item.title: Malaysia's Healthcare System: A 'Ticking Bomb' — 2.83% of GDP While Countries Spend Double
item.description:
Said by: P4H Network / University of Malaya Working Paper / The Star

Category: Health

Date: 2025-09-08

📌 What Happened

Multiple independent analyses have declared Malaysia’s healthcare system a ’ticking bomb.’ Public health expenditure sits at just 2.83% of GDP in 2023, far below WHO-recommended levels and regional peers. The doctor-to-patient ratio of 1:417 masks the true crisis in the public sector, which handles 80% of hospital beds with 54% of doctors. The country is 11,000 specialists short. Junior doctors work 84-hour weeks.

item.title: T20 Families Now Using Public Hospitals — The Rich Can't Afford Private Healthcare Anymore
item.description:
Said by: Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations / The Star

Category: Health

Date: 2025-09-08

📌 What Happened

The Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (FOMCA) sounded alarms that even T20 families (top 20% income earners) are switching to public hospitals because private healthcare has become prohibitively expensive. FOMCA senior manager Saral James Maniam called it a ‘big red flag.’

🔥 Why It Matters

When Malaysia’s wealthiest citizens find private healthcare unaffordable, the entire healthcare financing model has collapsed. These families flood already-overwhelmed public hospitals, creating longer queues and worse outcomes for B40 and M40 patients who have no alternative. The system is experiencing a doom loop: rising private costs → T20 shift to public → public system overwhelmed → quality drops → nobody gets adequate care.

item.description:

item.title: [BM] Rang Undang-Undang Pembaharuan Bandar Nga Kor Ming Beri Seorang Menteri Kuasa Mengatasi Hak Milik — AP Sendiri Pun Memberontak
item.description:
Said by: Nga Kor Ming, Housing and Local Government Minister

Category: Housing

Date: 2025-08-25

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU

Pada Ogos 2025, Menteri Perumahan dan Kerajaan Tempatan Nga Kor Ming membentangkan Rang Undang-Undang Pembaharuan Bandar 2025, yang direka untuk mempercepatkan pembangunan semula perumahan bandar yang uzur. Rang undang-undang itu mencadangkan menurunkan ambang persetujuan untuk pembangunan semula — bermakna pemilik hartanah boleh dipaksa menjual atau berpindah walaupun tanpa persetujuan sebulat suara.

Bantahan datang serta-merta dan merentas parti. Pengkritik memanggil rang undang-undang itu “cacat, menyalahi undang-undang dan tanpa legitimasi,” menuduh Nga menumpukan terlalu banyak kuasa di tangan seorang menteri. Rang undang-undang itu membenarkan pembangunan semula diteruskan dengan hanya 80% persetujuan penduduk, mengatasi hak milik 20% yang selebihnya.

item.title: Nga Kor Ming's Urban Renewal Bill Gives One Minister Power to Override Property Rights — Even His Own MPs Revolt
item.description:
Said by: Nga Kor Ming, Housing and Local Government Minister

Category: Housing

Date: 2025-08-25

📌 WHAT HAPPENED

In August 2025, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming tabled the Urban Renewal Bill 2025, designed to fast-track redevelopment of ageing urban housing. The bill proposed lowering the consent threshold for redevelopment — meaning property owners could be forced to sell or relocate even without unanimous agreement.

The backlash was immediate and bipartisan. Critics called the bill “defective, unlawful and devoid of legitimacy,” accusing Nga of concentrating too much power in one minister’s hands. The bill would allow redevelopment to proceed with just 80% resident consent, overriding the property rights of the remaining 20%.

item.title: [BM] Tebus Guna Pulau Selatan Pulau Pinang — Musnahkan Mata Pencarian 4,000 Nelayan Demi Impian Pemaju
item.description:
Said by: Chow Kon Yeow, Penang Chief Minister / DAP

Category: Social

Date: 2025-08-20

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Projek tebus guna Pulau Selatan Pulau Pinang (PSI) — kini dijenamakan semula sebagai ‘Silicon Island’ — adalah pelan pembangunan mega kerajaan negeri pimpinan DAP untuk mencipta 930 hektar tanah buatan di luar pantai selatan Pulau Pinang. Sehingga Ogos 2025, 80 hektar telah ditebus guna. Projek ini asalnya tiga pulau, kemudian dikecilkan kepada satu selepas bantahan awam. Lebih 4,000 nelayan pesisir terjejas. Hanya RM11.7 juta telah dibayar kepada 791 nelayan di bawah Pelan Pengurusan Kesan Sosial, dan 118 daripada 295 nelayan aktif menerima bot dan enjin baru bernilai RM10 juta. Nelayan kalah dalam cabaran mahkamah terhadap kelulusan Penilaian Kesan Alam Sekitar.

item.title: Penang South Islands Reclamation — Destroying 4,000 Fishermen's Livelihoods for a Developer's Dream
item.description:
Said by: Chow Kon Yeow, Penang Chief Minister / DAP

Category: Social

Date: 2025-08-20

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: The Penang South Islands (PSI) reclamation project — now rebranded as ‘Silicon Island’ — is the DAP-led state government’s mega-development plan to create 930 hectares of artificial land off Penang’s southern coast. As of August 2025, 80 hectares had been reclaimed. The project was originally three islands, later downsized to one after public outcry. More than 4,000 coastal fishermen are affected. Only RM11.7 million has been paid to 791 fishermen under the Social Impact Management Plan, and 118 of 295 active fishermen received new boats and engines worth RM10 million. Fishermen lost their court challenge to the Environmental Impact Assessment approval.

item.title: [BM] Krisis K-Pod Dan Vape Dalam Kalangan Belia — Wabak Dadah Baru Sementara Kerajaan Lambat Bertindak
item.description:
Said by: DPM Ahmad Zahid / AADK

Category: Health

Date: 2025-08-10

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Krisis dadah baru yang dahsyat sedang melanda sekolah dan komuniti Malaysia: K-pod dan vape berlapis dadah sintetik menjadi mekanisme penghantaran dadah pilihan belia Malaysia. Timbalan PM Ahmad Zahid mengakui keadaan berada pada ’tahap kritikal,’ dengan kes penyalahgunaan dadah melonjak 32.5% dari 2023 ke 2024 dan perangsang jenis amfetamina terlibat dalam lebih 70% kes.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Fenomena K-pod — kartrij vape berlapis dadah sintetik — amat berbahaya kerana ia menyamarkan penggunaan dadah sebagai vape biasa, menjadikan pengesanan oleh ibu bapa dan guru hampir mustahil. Platform media sosial telah menjadi saluran pengedaran, dengan pengedar mengiklan melalui Telegram dan TikTok.

item.title: K-Pods and Vape Crisis Among Youth — New Drug Epidemic While Government Plays Catch-Up
item.description:
Said by: DPM Ahmad Zahid / AADK

Category: Health

Date: 2025-08-10

📌 What Happened

A devastating new drug crisis is sweeping through Malaysian schools and communities: K-pods and synthetic drug-laced vapes are becoming the drug delivery mechanism of choice for young Malaysians. Deputy PM Ahmad Zahid acknowledged the situation was at a ‘critical level,’ with drug abuse cases surging 32.5% from 2023 to 2024 and amphetamine-type stimulants involved in over 70% of cases.

item.title: [BM] Institut Keamanan Toda: Anwar 'Jadikan Dasar Berasaskan Kaum LEBIH BURUK, Bukan Lebih Baik' — Cuba Mengatasi Islamis Dalam Pengislaman

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Ini adalah institut penyelidikan keamanan antarabangsa yang menyatakan bahawa PM Malaysia yang kononnya reformis sedang MEMBURUKKAN diskriminasi kaum, bukan mengurangkannya. Sistem dasar berasaskan kaum yang telah dilembagakan — yang digambarkan sebagai ‘membunuh merit, menyekat persaingan dan inovasi, membiakkan rasa tidak puas hati minoriti, dan melahirkan kronisme dengan mencipta elit Melayu kaya tanpa berbuat banyak untuk Melayu miskin’ — sedang diperkukuh bukannya direformasi di bawah Anwar.

item.title: Toda Peace Institute: Anwar 'Making Race-Based Policies WORSE, Not Better' — Trying to Out-Islamise the Islamists
item.description:
Said by: Toda Peace Institute Analysis

Category: Social

Date: 2025-08-01

📌 What Happened

The Toda Peace Institute published a comprehensive analysis titled ‘The Many Wars of Malaysia’s Anwar Ibrahim,’ concluding that Anwar ‘isn’t just reluctant to disturb the status quo; he is in fact making it worse by trying to out-Islamize the Islamists with gestures, policies and statements that the minorities find deeply worrying.’

🔥 Why It Matters

This is an international peace research institute saying that Malaysia’s supposedly reformist PM is WORSENING racial discrimination, not reducing it. The institutionalised system of race-based policies — described as ‘killing off merit, stifling competition and innovation, breeding minority resentments, and spawning cronyism by creating a rich Malay elite without doing much for poor Malays’ — is being strengthened rather than reformed under Anwar.

The Facts

Fact: Between 2022 and 2024, 705 doctors and 1,394 nurses with over five years of service resigned from public hospitals.

Fact: The Malaysian Medical Association called for the complete abolition of the contract system, which locks doctors into 3+2+2+4 year contracts with no job security.

item.title: [BM] GLC Sebagai Tempat Buang Politik — 47.5 Lantikan Setahun, Lebih Banyak Daripada Mahathir 2.0
item.description:
Said by: IDEAS Think Tank Research

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-07-04

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Penyelidikan badan pemikir IDEAS mendapati kerajaan Anwar melantik purata 47.5 lantikan politik setahun ke Syarikat Berkaitan Kerajaan (GLC) dan badan berkanun — melebihi kadar Mahathir 2.0 sebanyak 43 setahun dan jauh melebihi matlamat lantikan berasaskan merit. Sebanyak 238 lantikan politik didokumenkan sepanjang tahun-tahun pertama Anwar.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

GLC mengawal bahagian besar ekonomi Malaysia — Petronas, Khazanah, TNB, Telekom, MAHB, dan berpuluh-puluh lagi. Apabila jawatan lembaga pengarah diisi berdasarkan kesetiaan politik dan bukannya kecekapan, akibatnya besar: keputusan strategik yang lemah, rasuah, dan salah urus. Setiap lantikan politik yang kurang kemahiran untuk peranan mereka merugikan ekonomi dari segi kecekapan, inovasi, dan nilai pemegang saham.

item.title: [BM] Reformasi Perkhidmatan Awam: Tiga Tahun Bercakap, Sifar Perubahan Struktur — 1.6 Juta Birokrat Tidak Disentuh
item.description:
Said by: IDEAS / Public Policy Analysts

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-07-04

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Anwar Ibrahim memasuki pejabat menjanjikan reformasi perkhidmatan awam menyeluruh — pemodenan, meritokrasi, mengecilkan birokrasi yang gemuk yang memakan bahagian besar belanjawan negara. Tiga tahun kemudian, perkhidmatan awam kekal pada dasarnya tidak berubah: 1.3-1.6 juta pekerja (tidak termasuk polis dan tentera), 90% Bumiputera, memakan kira-kira 40% daripada jumlah perbelanjaan mengurus kerajaan dalam gaji dan pencen.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Badan pemikir IDEAS mendapati kerajaan Anwar sebenarnya meningkatkan lantikan politik ke GLC dan badan berkanun, purata 47.5 setahun — melebihi kadar Mahathir 2.0 sebanyak 43 setahun. Birokrasi yang gemuk bermakna Malaysia membelanjakan lebih banyak untuk gaji penjawat awam berbanding perbelanjaan pembangunan. Kewajipan pencen terus membengkak tanpa reformasi struktur.

item.title: Civil Service Reform: Three Years of Talk, Zero Structural Change — 1.6 Million Bureaucrats Untouched
item.description:
Said by: IDEAS / Public Policy Analysts

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-07-04

📌 What Happened

Anwar Ibrahim entered office promising sweeping civil service reform — modernisation, meritocracy, right-sizing a bloated bureaucracy that consumes a massive share of the national budget. Three years later, the civil service remains essentially unchanged: 1.3-1.6 million employees (excluding police and military), 90% Bumiputera, consuming approximately 40% of total government operating expenditure in salaries and pensions.

🔥 Why It Matters

IDEAS think tank found that the Anwar government actually increased political appointments to GLCs and statutory bodies, averaging 47.5 per year — exceeding even Mahathir 2.0’s rate of 43 per year. The bloated bureaucracy means Malaysia spends more on civil servant wages than on development spending. Pension obligations continue to balloon with no structural reform.

A total of 238 political appointments were documented across Anwar’s first years.

item.title: [BM] CSIS Isytihar 'Kematian Reformasi' — Gerakan Anwar Sendiri Diisytihar Mati Oleh Badan Pemikir Washington
item.description:
Said by: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-06-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), salah satu badan pemikir dasar paling berpengaruh di Washington, menerbitkan analisis yang memusnahkan bertajuk ‘Kematian Reformasi: Anwar Ibrahim, UMNO, dan Pengkhianatan Sebuah Gerakan.’ Artikel itu berhujah bahawa identiti politik Anwar telah ‘semakin ditakrifkan oleh kompromi yang beliau buat untuk memastikan kedudukannya dalam kerajaan.’

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Reformasi bukan sekadar gerakan politik — ia adalah janji generasi. Berjuta-juta rakyat Malaysia, daripada pelajar universiti hingga keluarga kelas pekerja, melaburkan berdekad harapan, bantahan, dan pengorbanan dalam kepercayaan bahawa Anwar Ibrahim mewakili politik yang berbeza secara asasi. CSIS mengisytiharkannya mati bukan retorik pembangkang — ia adalah keputusan pertubuhan dasar antarabangsa.

Date: 2025-06-01

Pasaran mata wang — yang menghimpunkan pertimbangan kolektif ribuan pelabur dan penganalisis — pada dasarnya mengundi tidak percaya terhadap asas ekonomi Malaysia.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Kelemahan ringgit membawa kesan langsung kepada rakyat Malaysia biasa: barangan import menjadi lebih mahal (menyumbang kepada inflasi makanan yang dirasai rakyat tetapi tidak dicerminkan sepenuhnya oleh statistik rasmi), kos pendidikan luar negara meningkat, dan penghijrahan otak semakin pesat kerana profesional Malaysia mendapati kemahiran mereka bernilai berlipat ganda di negara mata wang lebih kukuh.

item.title: [BM] Krisis Persaraan KWSP — Purata Baki RM47,600 Pada Umur 55 Bermakna KEMISKINAN Di Hari Tua
item.description:
Said by: EPF Data / Retirement Adequacy Studies

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-06-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Data KWSP secara konsisten menunjukkan majoriti rakyat Malaysia mempunyai simpanan persaraan yang sangat tidak mencukupi. Baki median pada umur 55 (umur pengeluaran wajib) adalah kira-kira RM47,600 — cukup untuk bertahan kira-kira 5 tahun pada RM800/bulan, jauh di bawah mana-mana garis kemiskinan yang munasabah. Dasar kerajaan membenarkan pengeluaran KWSP berulang (Akaun 3 menyaksikan RM14.79 bilion dikeluarkan oleh 4.63 juta pencarum) telah mempercepatkan kehabisan dana persaraan.

item.title: [BM] Pengumuman FDI Lawan Pekerjaan Sebenar — Angka RM Nampak Hebat, Tapi Mana Pekerjaan Untuk Rakyat Malaysia?
item.description:
Said by: MIDA / Economic Analysts

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-06-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Kerajaan kerap mengumumkan angka Pelaburan Langsung Asing (FDI) yang besar — berbilion ringgit dalam komitmen daripada gergasi teknologi, pengeluar dan pengendali pusat data. Pengumuman ini menjana tajuk berita yang mengagumkan. Walau bagaimanapun, jurang antara FDI yang diumumkan dan pelaburan sebenar yang direalisasikan, dan antara pelaburan dan pekerjaan sebenar rakyat Malaysia, kekal ketara.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Pengumuman FDI adalah kemenangan PR yang mudah — anda berdiri di sebelah CEO asing, tandatangan MOU, dan umumkan berbilion. Tetapi FDI diluluskan ≠ FDI direalisasikan (banyak projek ditangguh atau dibatalkan). FDI direalisasikan ≠ pekerjaan rakyat Malaysia (banyak pelaburan berintensif modal dengan pekerjaan minimum, atau menggaji pakar asing). Dan pekerjaan yang diwujudkan sering bukan jawatan berkualiti tinggi, bergaji baik yang menangani cabaran pengangguran dan genangan gaji Malaysia.

item.title: [BM] Perangkap Kebergantungan Buruh Asing — Ekonomi Tak Boleh Berfungsi Tanpa Pekerja Yang Malaysia Layan Macam Barang Buangan
item.description:
Said by: Labour Economists / ILO

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-06-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Malaysia kekal sangat bergantung kepada pekerja asing — dianggarkan 2-3 juta berdokumen dan mungkin berjuta lagi tanpa dokumen — dalam sektor kritikal termasuk pembinaan, pembuatan, pertanian, dan perkhidmatan. Dasar pekerja asing kerajaan berayun antara liberalisasi dan sekatan berdasarkan angin politik dan bukannya perancangan ekonomi, mewujudkan ketidaktentuan kronik bagi majikan dan pekerja.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Kebergantungan buruh asing mendedahkan kegagalan Malaysia untuk bergerak naik rantaian nilai — ekonomi masih bergantung secara struktur kepada buruh murah yang boleh dieksploitasi dan bukannya automasi, teknologi, dan pekerja domestik berkemahiran. Kebergantungan ini menekan gaji tempatan, membolehkan eksploitasi, dan mewujudkan ketegangan sosial.

The government’s policy of allowing repeated EPF withdrawals (Account 3 saw RM14.79 billion withdrawn by 4.63 million contributors) has accelerated retirement fund depletion.

item.title: FDI Announcements vs Actual Jobs — RM Numbers Look Great, But Where Are the Jobs for Malaysians?
item.description:
Said by: MIDA / Economic Analysts

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-06-01

📌 What Happened

The government regularly announces massive Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) figures — billions of ringgit in commitments from tech giants, manufacturers, and data centre operators. These announcements generate impressive headlines. However, the gap between announced FDI and actual realised investment, and between investment and actual Malaysian employment, remains significant.

🔥 Why It Matters

FDI announcements are easy PR wins — you stand next to a foreign CEO, sign an MOU, and announce billions. But approved FDI ≠ realised FDI (many projects are delayed or cancelled). Realised FDI ≠ Malaysian jobs (many investments are capital-intensive with minimal employment, or employ foreign specialists). And the jobs that are created are often not the high-quality, well-paying positions that address Malaysia’s unemployment and wage stagnation challenges.

item.title: Foreign Labour Dependency Trap — Economy Can't Function Without Workers Malaysia Treats Like Disposable Parts
item.description:
Said by: Labour Economists / ILO

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-06-01

📌 What Happened

Malaysia remains heavily dependent on foreign workers — estimated at 2-3 million documented and possibly millions more undocumented — in critical sectors including construction, manufacturing, agriculture, and services. The government’s foreign worker policy oscillates between liberalisation and restriction based on political winds rather than economic planning, creating chronic uncertainty for both employers and workers.

🔥 Why It Matters

Foreign worker dependency reveals Malaysia’s failure to move up the value chain — the economy is still structurally reliant on cheap, exploitable labour rather than automation, technology, and skilled domestic workers. This dependency suppresses local wages, enables exploitation, and creates social tensions.

item.title: Ringgit Weakness Persists Despite GDP Growth — Currency Doesn't Believe Anwar's Economic Story
item.description:
Said by: BNM / Currency Markets

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-06-01

📌 What Happened

Despite the government’s optimistic GDP growth narrative, the Malaysian ringgit has remained persistently weak against the US dollar and regional currencies, hovering around historically low levels. The currency markets — which aggregate the collective judgment of thousands of investors and analysts — are essentially voting no-confidence on Malaysia’s economic fundamentals.

🔥 Why It Matters

The weak ringgit has direct consequences for ordinary Malaysians: imported goods become more expensive (contributing to the food inflation that rakyat experience but official statistics undercount), overseas education costs more, and the brain drain accelerates as Malaysian professionals find their skills worth multiples more in stronger-currency countries.

item.title: [BM] Rekod 236 Tan Syabu Dirampas Di Rantau — Malaysia Hab Transit Utama
item.description:
Said by: UNODC Report 2025

Category: Health

Date: 2025-05-28

UNODC reported a record 236 tons of methamphetamine seized in East and Southeast Asia in 2024, up 24% from 2023. Malaysia busted its largest-ever maritime drug trafficking ring — 18+ tonnes worth RM375M. Drug use is increasing among older demographics. Government approved a ‘communication plan’ — not enforcement reform. This matters because Malaysia abolished mandatory death for drug trafficking, then watched seizures hit record highs. The government’s response to a worsening drug crisis was a ‘communication plan’ — essentially a PR strategy instead of structural enforcement reform. Malaysia sits on a major trafficking corridor and its ports are clearly being exploited. Record seizures can mean better enforcement or a bigger problem — and when the UNODC says the regional supply is surging 24% year-on-year, it’s the latter. A government that responds to a drug tsunami with a communications strategy is not serious about the problem. Sources: UNODC | Vietnam Plus

His resignation came hours after Economy Minister Rafizi Ramli also resigned — both following their defeats in PKR’s internal party elections five days earlier.

Nik Nazmi lost his PKR vice-president position and said he could no longer serve as minister without a full party mandate. “Being a minister can trap you in a ‘bubble’ — with privileges, security escorts, and protocols at every event,” he said. “I believe that becoming too attached to such a lifestyle can be dangerous.”

item.description:
Said by: Enforcement Agencies / Media Investigations

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-03-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Sistem imigresen Malaysia kekal dibelenggu sindiket rasuah yang mengeksploitasi berjuta pekerja asing, mengekstrak berbilion ringgit melalui levi haram, penipuan dokumen, dan pemerdagangan buruh. Walaupun janji kerajaan berulang kali untuk membersihkan sistem, siasatan terus mendedahkan rangkaian yang berakar umbi melibatkan pegawai imigresen, ejen buruh, dan majikan.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Pekerja asing — dianggarkan 2-3 juta berdokumen dan berjuta lagi tanpa dokumen — membayar yuran pengambilan yang melampau, sering menjadi hamba terikat yang terperangkap dalam kitaran ikatan hutang. Sistem levi pekerja asing pelbagai peringkat telah berulang kali ditangguhkan, mewujudkan ketidaktentuan yang menguntungkan perantara rasuah. Laporan Pemerdagangan Orang Jabatan Negara AS telah secara konsisten menandakan isu buruh paksa Malaysia, terutamanya dalam pertanian perladangan, pembinaan, dan pembuatan.

item.title: Immigration Corruption Syndicates Thrive — Foreign Worker Exploitation a Multi-Billion Ringgit Industry
item.description:
Said by: Enforcement Agencies / Media Investigations

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-03-01

📌 What Happened

Malaysia’s immigration system remains plagued by corruption syndicates that exploit millions of foreign workers, extracting billions of ringgit through illegal levies, document fraud, and labour trafficking. Despite repeated government promises to clean up the system, investigations continue to reveal deeply entrenched networks involving immigration officials, labour agents, and employers.

🔥 Why It Matters

Foreign workers — numbering an estimated 2-3 million documented and millions more undocumented — pay exorbitant recruitment fees, often becoming indentured servants trapped in cycles of debt bondage. The multi-tier foreign worker levy system has been delayed repeatedly, creating uncertainty that benefits corrupt intermediaries. US State Department Trafficking in Persons reports have consistently flagged Malaysia’s forced labour issues, particularly in plantation agriculture, construction, and manufacturing.

item.title: [BM] Anwar Serang Balik Pengkritik Yang Kata Dia Terlalu Banyak Melancong — 'Mereka Tak Faham Kerja Keras'
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-02-27

PM Terbang Yang Tak Boleh Terima Kritikan

Apabila rakyat Malaysia mempersoalkan mengapa PM mereka sentiasa di luar negara sementara krisis domestik meningkat, respons Anwar bukan empati — ia kemarahan. Beliau menyerang pengkritik, berkata mereka “jelas tidak menyedari kerja keras” yang terlibat dalam perjalanan luar negara.

Fakta

Fakta: Anwar mempertahankan jadual perjalanan luar negaranya yang meluas, menolak pengkritik sebagai tidak berpengetahuan.

item.title: [BM] East Asia Forum: 'Aspirasi Reformasi Bertembung Dengan Realiti Politik Pada 2024'
item.description:
Said by: Kai Ostwald, University of British Columbia

Date: 2025-02-27

Yet political turbulence — driven by identity-based populism and an unwieldy coalition — continued to constrain domestic reforms.’ Sources: https://eastasiaforum.org/2025/02/27/malaysias-reform-aspirations-clashed-with-political-realities-in-2024/

item.title: Anwar Hits Back at Critics Who Say He Travels Too Much — 'They Don't Understand Hard Work'
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-02-27

The Jet-Setting PM Who Can’t Take Criticism

When Malaysians questioned why their PM was constantly abroad while domestic crises mounted, Anwar’s response was not empathy — it was indignation. He hit out at critics, saying they were “clearly unaware of the hard work” that goes into overseas trips.

The Facts

Fact: Anwar defended his extensive overseas travel schedule, dismissing critics as uninformed.

item.title: [BM] Anwar Berpatah Balik Soal Garis Panduan Muslim Di Majlis Bukan Islam Selepas Tentangan Hebat
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister

Category: Religion

Date: 2025-02-07

Cadang Perpecahan Dahulu, Kemudian Berlagak Tak Tahu

Pada awal Februari 2025, kerajaan Anwar mencadangkan garis panduan terbitan JAKIM yang menyekat penyertaan Muslim di majlis keagamaan bukan Islam. Tentangan datang serta-merta dan dahsyat. Dalam beberapa hari, Anwar membatalkan cadangan itu, berkata “tiada keperluan” kerana umat Islam “sudah sepatutnya tahu” peraturan.

Fakta

Fakta: Pada 5 Februari 2025, Menteri Hal Ehwal Agama Mohd Na’im Mokhtar mengumumkan garis panduan baru yang mewajibkan penganjur mendapat kebenaran pihak berkuasa Islam sebelum menjemput Muslim, melarang majlis berhampiran masjid, dan mengharamkan “propaganda agama.”

item.title: [BM] Anwar Undur Garis Panduan Muslim Untuk Acara Bukan Islam Selepas Tentangan Hebat
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister

Category: Religion

Date: 2025-02-07

Cadangkan Perpecahan Dahulu, Kemudian Berlagak Tak Buat

Pada awal Februari 2025, kerajaan Anwar mencadangkan garis panduan terbitan JAKIM yang menyekat penyertaan Muslim di acara keagamaan bukan Islam. Tentangan datang serta-merta dan bertubi-tubi. Dalam masa beberapa hari, Anwar membatalkan cadangan itu, berkata “tiada keperluan” kerana orang Islam “sepatutnya sudah tahu” peraturannya.

Fakta

Fakta: Pada 5 Februari 2025, Menteri Hal Ehwal Agama Mohd Na’im Mokhtar mengumumkan garis panduan baharu yang memerlukan penganjur mendapatkan kebenaran pihak berkuasa Islam sebelum menjemput umat Islam, melarang acara berhampiran masjid, dan mengharamkan “propaganda agama.”

item.title: Anwar Backtracks on Muslim Guidelines for Non-Muslim Events After Fierce Backlash
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, Prime Minister

Category: Religion

Date: 2025-02-07

First Propose Division, Then Pretend You Didn’t

In early February 2025, Anwar’s government proposed JAKIM-issued guidelines restricting Muslim participation at non-Muslim religious events. The backlash was immediate and ferocious. Within days, Anwar scrapped the proposal, saying “there is no need” because Muslims “should already know” the rules.

The Facts

Fact: On 5 February 2025, Religious Affairs Minister Mohd Na’im Mokhtar announced new guidelines requiring organisers to seek permission from Islamic authorities before inviting Muslims, banning events near mosques, and prohibiting “religious propaganda.”

item.title: [BM] Unit Propaganda J-Kom Terus Hidup — PH Kekalkan Jentera Yang Pernah Dikutuknya
item.description:
Said by: Fahmi Fadzil, Communications Minister

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-02-06

PH bubarkan JASA pada 2018 memanggilnya alat propaganda BN. Dihidupkan semula sebagai J-Kom dengan bajet RM85.5J. AP Hassan Abdul Karim memanggilnya ’lewah’ dan ‘jabatan propaganda untuk parti pemerintah.’

item.title: J-Kom Propaganda Unit Lives On — PH Keeps the Machine It Once Condemned
item.description:
Said by: Fahmi Fadzil, Communications Minister

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-02-06

PH dissolved JASA in 2018 calling it BN’s propaganda tool. Revived as J-Kom with RM85.5M budget. MP Hassan Abdul Karim called it ‘redundant’ and a ‘propaganda department for the ruling party.’

item.title: [BM] Najib Dapat Tahanan Rumah — 'Hukuman' Paling Selesa Dunia Untuk Kleptokrasi Terbesar Dunia
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim Administration / Pardons Board

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-02-02

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Bekas PM Najib Razak, disabitkan kesalahan rasuah dalam skandal 1MDB yang merompak berbilion daripada rakyat Malaysia, mendapat hukuman dipotong separuh melalui pengampunan diraja dan seterusnya dipindahkan ke tahanan rumah di kediamannya yang mewah di Kuala Lumpur. Orang yang disabitkan mencuri daripada rakyat kini menjalani ‘hukuman’ di rumah agam.

🔥 Kenapa Ia Penting

1MDB adalah kes kleptokrasi terbesar dalam sejarah. DOJ Amerika Syarikat menganggarkan $4.5 bilion telah diselewengkan. Malaysia MASIH membayar hutangnya — RM42 bilion telah dibayar setakat ini, beban keseluruhan RM50 bilion. Rakyat biasa menanggung kos ini melalui perkhidmatan awam yang berkurangan, cukai lebih tinggi, dan kekangan fiskal. Orang yang bertanggungjawab hidup selesa sementara mangsanya membayar hutangnya.

item.title: Najib Gets House Arrest — The World's Most Comfortable 'Punishment' for the World's Biggest Kleptocracy
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim Administration / Pardons Board

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-02-02

📌 What Happened

Former PM Najib Razak, convicted of corruption in the 1MDB scandal that looted billions from the Malaysian public, had his sentence halved by a royal pardon and was subsequently transferred to house arrest at his luxurious Kuala Lumpur residence. The man convicted of stealing from the rakyat now serves ’time’ in a mansion.

🔥 Why It Matters

1MDB was the largest kleptocracy case in history. US DOJ estimated $4.5 billion was misappropriated. Malaysia is STILL paying the debt — RM42 billion paid so far, RM50 billion total burden. Ordinary Malaysians bear this cost through reduced public services, higher taxes, and fiscal constraints. The man responsible lives in comfort while his victims pay his debts.

item.title: [BM] Gaji Minimum RM1,700 — Pekerja Masih Tak Boleh Berunding, Majikan Tangguh 6 Bulan
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, PM / Ministry of Human Resources

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-02-01

Gaji minimum RM1,700 berkuat kuasa Feb 2025 tetapi hanya untuk syarikat 5+ pekerja. Penguatkuasaan penuh ditangguhkan ke Ogos 2025. Fulcrum nyatakan ‘kebanyakan pekerja masih tiada kuasa berunding.’

item.title: Minimum Wage RM1,700 — Workers Still Can't Bargain, Employers Defer 6 Months
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim, PM / Ministry of Human Resources

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-02-01

RM1,700 minimum wage came into effect Feb 2025 but only for companies with 5+ employees. Full enforcement deferred to Aug 2025. Fulcrum noted ‘most workers still lack bargaining power.’

item.title: [BM] Skor CPI Mendatar Di 50 — Sama Seperti Ketika Kemuncak Skandal 1MDB 2015
item.description:
Said by: Transparency International / Rafizi Ramli

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-01-28

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Indeks Persepsi Rasuah Malaysia tersekat di 50 mata dan ke-57 global pada 2023 dan 2024 — sama dengan skor ketika kemuncak skandal 1MDB pada 2015. Rafizi sendiri memberi amaran ini ‘berlaku walaupun pendirian toleransi sifar Anwar terhadap rasuah.’

🔥 Kenapa Ia Penting

CPI adalah penanda aras antarabangsa paling banyak dirujuk untuk rasuah. Selepas dua tahun retorik ’toleransi sifar’ Anwar, skor Malaysia tidak bergerak satu mata pun. Negara ini dilihat sama rasuah seperti ketika Najib menyedut berbilion melalui 1MDB. Ini bukan kesan ketinggalan — CPI mencerminkan persepsi semasa berdasarkan tinjauan pemimpin perniagaan dan pakar.

item.title: CPI Score Flatlines at 50 — Same as During Peak 1MDB Scandal in 2015
item.description:
Said by: Transparency International / Rafizi Ramli

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-01-28

📌 What Happened

Malaysia’s Corruption Perceptions Index stuck at 50 points and 57th globally in both 2023 and 2024 — identical to the score during the peak 1MDB scandal in 2015. Rafizi himself warned this is ‘happening despite Anwar’s zero-tolerance stance on corruption.’

🔥 Why It Matters

The CPI is the most widely cited international benchmark for corruption. After two years of Anwar’s ‘zero tolerance’ rhetoric, Malaysia’s score has not moved a single point. The country is perceived as exactly as corrupt as it was when Najib was siphoning billions through 1MDB. This is not a lag effect — the CPI reflects current perceptions based on surveys of business leaders and experts.

item.title: [BM] Penswastaan MAHB — Pengarah Bebas Kata 'Tidak Adil' Tetapi Teruskan Juga
item.description:
Said by: Gateway Development Alliance / Khazanah

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-01-24

Pengarah bebas MAHB sendiri menolak pengambilalihan RM11/saham sebagai ’tidak adil dan tidak munasabah.’ Masyarakat sivil membantah penglibatan GIP BlackRock atas kebimbangan boikot Palestin. MAHB tetap dinyahsenarai.

item.title: MAHB Privatisation — Independent Directors Say 'Not Fair' But Proceed Anyway
item.description:
Said by: Gateway Development Alliance / Khazanah

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-01-24

MAHB’s own independent directors rejected the RM11/share takeover as ‘unfair and unreasonable.’ Civil society protested BlackRock’s GIP involvement amid Palestine boycott concerns. MAHB delisted anyway.

item.description:

Category: Economy

Perjalanan tanpa tol musim perayaan dihentikan secara senyap. PH janji mansuhkan tol sepenuhnya di PRU15. Sebaliknya, tol masih kekal, kerajaan bayar RM591J untuk bekukan kadar sedia ada, dan kini habis sudah keistimewaan kecil perayaan.

item.title: Festive Season Toll-Free Travel Discontinued — Even This Small Perk Gone
item.description:
Said by: Government of Malaysia

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-01-21

Festive toll-free travel quietly discontinued. PH promised to abolish tolls entirely in GE15. Instead, tolls still stand, government pays RM591M to freeze existing rates, and now even the small festive perk is gone.

item.title: [BM] Human Rights Watch: 'Kemerosotan Hak Di Bawah Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim'
item.description:
Said by: Human Rights Watch

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-16

Reformis Yang Mundur Soal Hak

Pada Januari 2025, Human Rights Watch mengeluarkan penilaian pedas: “Kemerosotan Hak Di Bawah Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.” CIVICUS mengkadarkan ruang sivil Malaysia sebagai “terhalang.”

Fakta

Fakta: Penyelidik Asia HRW Shayna Bauchner berkata: “Dalam tahun pertama memegang jawatan, Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim mengkhianati ikrar reformasi yang dibuat kepada pengundi Malaysia supaya beliau dapat mengekalkan gabungannya.”

Fakta: CIVICUS melaporkan undang-undang yang menyekat — terutama CMA dan Akta Hasutan — terus digunakan untuk membungkam perbezaan pendapat dalam talian dan mengganggu pembela hak asasi manusia.

item.title: Human Rights Watch: 'Rights Backslide Under Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim'
item.description:
Said by: Human Rights Watch

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-16

The Reformist Who Backslid on Rights

In January 2025, Human Rights Watch issued a damning assessment: “Rights Backslide Under Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.” CIVICUS rated Malaysia’s civic space as “obstructed.”

The Facts

Fact: HRW’s Asia researcher Shayna Bauchner said: “In his first year in office, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim betrayed the reform pledges he made to Malaysian voters so he could hold his coalition together.”

item.title: [BM] Akta Hasutan MASIH Tidak Dimansuhkan — PH Janji Menghapuskannya Pada 2018 Dan 2022, Kemudian Menggunakannya
item.description:
Said by: Lawyers for Liberty / Article 19 / Bar Council

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Akta Hasutan 1948 — undang-undang era penjajah yang PH secara jelas berjanji memansuhkan dalam manifesto pilihan raya 2018 dan 2022 — kekal beroperasi sepenuhnya di bawah kerajaan Anwar. Bukan sahaja ia tidak dimansuhkan, ia sedang digunakan secara aktif terhadap pengkritik kerajaan. Aktivis Chegubard didakwa di bawah Akta tersebut atas siaran media sosial mengenai kasino Forest City.

item.title: [BM] Bajet Pendidikan Tinggi Terus Menyusut — Dari 6.8% Pada 2010 Kepada Hanya 4.3% Pada 2025
item.description:
Said by: New Mandala / Academic Analysis

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Bajet pendidikan tinggi Malaysia telah jatuh dari 6.8% daripada jumlah bajet negara pada 2010 kepada hanya 4.3% pada 2025, dengan titik terendah pada 3.9% pada 2023. Sementara itu, enrolmen tertiari berada pada hanya 42.57% — jauh di bawah 93% Singapura dan purata global 51.98%. Analisis akademik menggambarkan “jurang yang semakin melebar antara wacana reformis dan komitmen kewangan sebenar” terhadap pendidikan di bawah PH.

item.title: [BM] Enrolmen Tertiari Malaysia Pada 42.57% — Di Bawah Purata Global, Jauh Ketinggalan 93% Singapura
item.description:
Said by: Academic Research / UNESCO Data

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

Hanya 42.57% rakyat Malaysia yang layak mendaftar dalam pendidikan tertiari — di bawah purata global 51.98%. Singapura pada 93%, AS pada 88%. Lebih 10,000 pelajar SPM (2.6%) tidak menduduki peperiksaan.

item.title: [BM] Ibu Tunggal Dalam Kemiskinan — 300,000+ Keluarga Diketuai Wanita Hidup Di Bawah Garis Kemiskinan
item.description:
Said by: Women’s Ministry / DOSM Data

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Dianggarkan 300,000+ isi rumah ibu tunggal di Malaysia hidup pada atau di bawah garis kemiskinan, menghadapi sokongan kerajaan yang tidak mencukupi, diskriminasi pekerjaan, dan infrastruktur penjagaan kanak-kanak yang tidak memadai. Ibu tunggal diwakili secara tidak seimbang dalam kalangan isi rumah B40 dan menghadapi halangan termasuk akses terhad kepada perumahan mampu milik, penjagaan kesihatan, dan latihan kemahiran.

item.title: [BM] Jho Low MASIH Bebas Selepas 8 Tahun — Buronan Paling Dikehendaki Malaysia Hidup Selesa Entah Di Mana
item.description:
Said by: Interpol / MACC / DOJ

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Sehingga 2025, Low Taek Jho (Jho Low) — tokoh utama skandal 1MDB — masih bebas walaupun notis merah Interpol, waran tangkap antarabangsa, dan pertuduhan di pelbagai bidang kuasa. Tiga kerajaan Malaysia berbeza gagal mendapatkan ekstradisinya. Anwar jadikan akauntabiliti 1MDB janji utamanya, namun tiada kemajuan ketara dalam mengesan atau mengekstradisi Jho Low. Laporan menyebut beliau tinggal di China atau Macau, tetapi kerajaan Malaysia tidak mendedahkan sebarang usaha diplomatik untuk mendapatkan pulangannya.

item.title: [BM] Jurang Digital Berterusan — Komuniti Luar Bandar Masih Tanpa Internet Yang Boleh Dipercayai Sementara Kerajaan Bercakap 5G
item.description:
Said by: MCMC / Rural Development Ministry

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Sehingga awal 2025, berjuta-juta rakyat Malaysia di kawasan luar bandar Sabah, Sarawak dan pantai timur Semenanjung Malaysia masih tidak mempunyai akses internet yang boleh dipercayai. Sementara kerajaan membelanjakan berbilion untuk bencana rangkaian dwi 5G DNB lawan Telekom Malaysia, program JENDELA untuk menambah baik infrastruktur digital asas menghadapi kelewatan dan jurang liputan. Pelajar di sekolah luar bandar sangat terpinggir semasa pembelajaran jarak jauh COVID-19, dan jurang digital tidak mengecil secara bermakna sejak itu. Data SKMM sendiri menunjukkan jurang ketersambungan antara kawasan bandar dan luar bandar kekal ketara, dengan banyak sekolah luar bandar bergantung kepada sambungan satelit yang tidak stabil atau tiada ketersambungan langsung.

item.title: [BM] Jurang Gaji Gender Kekal 6-9% — Wanita Kerja Lebih Dapat Gaji Kurang, Kerajaan Tidak Buat Apa
item.description:
Said by: DOSM / Talentcorp Data

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Walaupun kerajaan Anwar mempunyai wanita terkemuka dalam kabinet dan retorik sesekali tentang kesaksamaan gender, jurang gaji gender Malaysia kekal degil pada anggaran 6-9% merentasi sektor, dengan jurang yang jauh lebih besar dalam industri tertentu. Wanita menanggung beban yang tidak seimbang dalam kerja penjagaan tanpa gaji, menghadapi penalti kerjaya kerana keibuan, dan kurang diwakili dalam pengurusan kanan dan jawatan lembaga.

item.title: [BM] Kakitangan Awam Dapat Pencen Seumur Hidup, Pekerja Swasta Dapat EPF Yang Semakin Susut — Sistem Persaraan Dua Tingkat
item.description:
Said by: Public Finance Analysts / EPF

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-01-01

1.3-1.6M civil servants get defined-benefit pensions for life funded by taxpayers. 16M private sector workers rely on EPF with median balance of RM47,600 that runs out in 5 years. No government has had the courage to reform it because the civil service is a critical vote bank.

item.title: [BM] Kegagalan Tindakan Iklim — Ikrar Perjanjian Paris Malaysia Fantasi, Pelepasan Terus Meningkat
item.description:
Said by: Climate Action Tracker / Environmental Groups

Category: Other

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Walaupun menjadi penandatangan Perjanjian Paris dan membuat ikrar bercita-cita tinggi mengenai pengurangan pelepasan karbon, trajektori pelepasan sebenar Malaysia terus meningkat. Penebangan hutan berterusan, loji kuasa arang batu kekal beroperasi, penggunaan tenaga pusat data berkembang, dan kerajaan tidak menawarkan laluan yang boleh dipercayai untuk memenuhi komitmen iklim yang dinyatakannya.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Perubahan iklim sudah menjejaskan Malaysia melalui banjir yang lebih teruk (kemusnahan 2024), kemarau berpanjangan, paras laut yang meningkat mengancam komuniti pesisir, dan kehilangan biodiversiti. Negara ini serentak menjadi mangsa dan penyumbang — industri kelapa sawit dan penebangan hutannya adalah sumber pelepasan global yang ketara. Kegagalan bertindak atas iklim bukan sekadar dasar buruk — ia ancaman eksistensial kepada masa depan Malaysia.

item.title: [BM] Kekurangan Guru Di Sekolah Luar Bandar — Anak Kampung Dapat Pendidikan Kelas Kedua
item.description:
Said by: Education Ministry / NUTP

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Sekolah luar bandar di seluruh Malaysia menghadapi kekurangan guru kronik dalam matematik, sains, dan bahasa Inggeris — tiga mata pelajaran paling kritikal untuk daya saing ekonomi. Komuniti orang asli di Sabah, Sarawak, dan penempatan Orang Asli menghadapi jurang paling teruk, dengan sesetengah sekolah langsung tiada guru berkelayakan untuk mata pelajaran utama. Kesatuan Perkhidmatan Perguruan Kebangsaan (NUTP) telah berulang kali membangkitkan isu ini. Kementerian Pendidikan mengakui kekurangan tetapi tidak melaksanakan pembaharuan struktur.

item.title: [BM] Kematian Jalan Raya Di Tahap Bencana — Malaysia Antara Jalan Paling Maut Di ASEAN, Jawapan Kerajaan: 'Kamera Laju'
item.description:
Said by: MIROS / WHO Road Safety Data

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Malaysia mencatat lebih 6,000 kematian jalan raya setahun — kira-kira 16 orang setiap hari. Penunggang motosikal merupakan bahagian terbesar kematian. Data WHO meletakkan Malaysia antara jalan paling maut di ASEAN dengan kadar kematian lalu lintas jauh melebihi purata global. Jawapan utama kerajaan adalah kamera laju, kempen penguatkuasaan berkala, dan program kesedaran. Tiada pembaharuan struktur keselamatan jalan raya, standard pelesenan, atau keperluan keselamatan kenderaan dilaksanakan di bawah PH.

item.title: [BM] Kepulauan Selatan Pulau Pinang: Projek Tebus Guna $14B Musnahkan Kawasan Tangkapan 6,000 Nelayan
item.description:
Said by: Penang State Government / SAM

Category: Other

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Projek Kepulauan Selatan Pulau Pinang (PSI) — asalnya tiga pulau buatan bernilai kira-kira $14 bilion — mengancam mata pencarian 6,000 nelayan, 51,184 tan tangkapan marin tahunan bernilai RM525 juta, dan 511 ladang akuakultur menjana RM1.67 bilion setahun. Selepas bantahan berterusan daripada komuniti nelayan dan kumpulan alam sekitar termasuk Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM), projek dikecilkan kepada satu pulau. Namun, pembinaan diteruskan, dan kesan asas terhadap kawasan tangkapan dan ekosistem marin kekal.

item.title: [BM] Krisis Kesihatan Mental Berputar — Bunuh Diri Dan Kemurungan Belia Melonjak Sementara Kerajaan Kurang Dana Perkhidmatan
item.description:
Said by: Health Ministry / WHO Data

Category: Health

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Malaysia menghadapi krisis kesihatan mental yang semakin mendalam, terutamanya dalam kalangan orang muda, dengan kadar kemurungan, kebimbangan, dan bunuh diri yang meningkat. Tinjauan Kesihatan dan Morbiditi Kebangsaan secara konsisten menunjukkan peningkatan yang membimbangkan dalam isu kesihatan mental, dengan hampir 3 daripada 10 rakyat Malaysia mengalami sejenis masalah kesihatan mental.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Belia terjejas secara tidak seimbang: tekanan media sosial, tekanan akademik, ketidaktentuan ekonomi dengan pengangguran belia 12.28%, dan kesan psikologi COVID-19 yang berlarutan telah mewujudkan ribut sempurna. Namun perkhidmatan kesihatan mental kerajaan kekal sangat kurang dana dan kurang kakitangan. Hospital awam menghadapi kekurangan pakar psikiatri dan ahli psikologi yang teruk, dengan masa menunggu berminggu-minggu atau berbulan-bulan.

item.title: [BM] Krisis Ketagihan Judi — 4D, Toto, Dan Pertaruhan Dalam Talian Musnahkan Keluarga Sementara Kerajaan Kutip Hasil
item.description:
Said by: Health Ministry / NGOs

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Malaysia menghadapi krisis ketagihan judi yang semakin meningkat didorong oleh outlet 4D dan Toto berlesen, pertaruhan sukan, dan ledakan platform judi dalam talian haram. Kerajaan mendapat keuntungan daripada judi melalui yuran pelesenan dan cukai permainan — mengutip berbilion setiap tahun daripada pengendali berlesen. Sementara itu, ketagihan judi memusnahkan keluarga berpendapatan rendah, dengan perkhidmatan rawatan kekal minimum berbanding skala masalah. Judi dalam talian telah meletup melebihi keupayaan penguatkuasaan SKMM.

item.title: [BM] Krisis Pinjaman PTPTN — Berjuta Berhutang Berbilion, Kadar Bayaran Balik Teruk, Graduan Terperangkap Dalam Hutang
item.description:
Said by: PTPTN / Auditor General Reports

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Perbadanan Tabung Pendidikan Tinggi Nasional (PTPTN) menghadapi krisis bayaran balik yang kronik, dengan berbilion ringgit pinjaman tertunggak dan kadar bayaran balik yang secara konsisten gagal mencapai sasaran. Berjuta graduan Malaysia menanggung hutang PTPTN yang menghadkan keupayaan mereka untuk menyimpan, melabur, atau membeli rumah. Kelestarian dana itu dipersoalkan tanpa reformasi besar.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Hutang PTPTN mewujudkan perangkap kemiskinan antara generasi: graduan memasuki tenaga kerja sudah berhutang, menghadapi ekonomi dengan pengangguran belia 12.28%, memperoleh gaji yang hampir tidak menanggung kos sara hidup (gaji minimum RM1,500), dan perlu membayar balik pinjaman pelajar sambil membina kehidupan. Ramai tidak mampu — sebab itulah kadar bayaran balik begitu rendah. Kitaran ini memakan dirinya sendiri: pendidikan tidak mampu → hutang → gaji rendah → tidak mampu bayar balik → isu kelayakan kredit → tidak mampu dapatkan gadai janji → status penyewa kekal.

item.title: [BM] Malaysia Enggan Ratifikasi ICERD — Anwar Tunduk Kepada Politik Perkauman Soal Perjanjian Hak Asasi Antarabangsa
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim Administration / Malay-Muslim Groups

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Malaysia kekal antara sedikit negara di dunia yang belum meratifikasi Konvensyen Antarabangsa Mengenai Penghapusan Segala Bentuk Diskriminasi Kaum (ICERD). Pada 2018, percubaan PH meratifikasi ICERD ditinggalkan selepas bantahan besar-besaran yang dipimpin kumpulan Melayu-Muslim yang berhujah ia akan menjejaskan keistimewaan Bumiputera. Anwar, pernah pemimpin progresif yang komited kepada kesamarataan, tidak menyentuh semula isu ini sejak menjadi PM.

item.title: [BM] Penghijrahan Otak Semakin Pantas — 1.86 Juta Rakyat Malaysia Telah Pergi, Dan Yang Terbaik Terus Meninggalkan
item.description:
Said by: World Bank / Talent Corporation Data

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-01-01

1.86 million Malaysians living abroad, disproportionately highly skilled. Public hospital doctors work 84-hour weeks for poverty wages. 11,000 specialist shortage directly linked to brain drain. Structural causes — race-based policies, low wages, poor governance — remain unaddressed.

item.title: [BM] Penyahutanan Kelapa Sawit Berterusan Tanpa Kawalan — Ikrar Alam Sekitar Lawan Keuntungan Ladang
item.description:
Said by: Environmental NGOs / SAM

Category: Other

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Walaupun komitmen Malaysia kepada perjanjian iklim antarabangsa dan matlamat pembangunan mampan, penyahutanan untuk ladang kelapa sawit terus merosakkan hutan hujan tropika antara yang tertua dan paling biodiversiti di Bumi. Skim pensijilan Minyak Sawit Mampan Malaysia (MSPO) dikritik NGO antarabangsa sebagai pencucian hijau yang tidak mencukupi. Kualiti air sungai Malaysia merosot — sungai bersih turun dari 486 ke 468 pada 2025. Sungai Perak bertukar biru akibat pelepasan perlombongan nadir bumi pada November 2025. Spesies terancam termasuk orang utan, gajah pygmy, dan harimau Malaya menghadapi habitat yang semakin mengecil.

item.title: [BM] Perkahwinan Kanak-Kanak MASIH Sah — PH Janji Hapuskannya, Kemudian Tidak Buat Apa Kerana 'Sensitiviti Islam'
item.description:
Said by: Sisters in Islam / UNICEF / Women’s Rights Groups

Category: Religion

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Walaupun bertahun-tahun kempen oleh pertubuhan hak wanita dan janji jelas daripada ahli politik PH, perkahwinan kanak-kanak kekal sah di Malaysia. Di bawah undang-undang keluarga Islam (bidang kuasa negeri), gadis semuda 16 tahun boleh berkahwin dengan kelulusan Mahkamah Syariah, dan dalam praktiknya, perkahwinan yang lebih muda telah didokumentasikan.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Perkahwinan kanak-kanak merampas pendidikan, kemerdekaan ekonomi, dan autonomi tubuh gadis. Ia dikaitkan dengan kadar keganasan rumah tangga yang lebih tinggi, kemiskinan, komplikasi kesihatan daripada kehamilan awal, dan kelemahan antara generasi. UNICEF telah berulang kali menggesa Malaysia menaikkan umur minimum perkahwinan kepada 18 tahun untuk semua.

item.title: [BM] Proton Masih Bergantung Pada Perlindungan Kerajaan — 40 Tahun 'Kereta Nasional' Dan Masih Tak Boleh Bersaing
item.description:
Said by: Automotive Industry Analysts

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Selepas 40 tahun dan berbilion dalam subsidi awam, pengecualian cukai, dan dasar perdagangan perlindungan, Proton masih tidak boleh bersaing di peringkat antarabangsa tanpa perlindungan kerajaan. Duti import yang tinggi — duti eksais sehingga 100% ke atas kereta asing — melambungkan harga kenderaan untuk 33 juta rakyat Malaysia. Kereta yang sama berharga separuh di Thailand atau Indonesia. Kerajaan Anwar tidak menunjukkan kecenderungan untuk mereformasi dasar perdagangan automotif atau menghapuskan perlindungan yang merugikan pengguna Malaysia berbilion setiap tahun.

item.title: [BM] SOSMA Masih Tidak Dimansuhkan — PH Guna Undang-Undang Keselamatan Yang Mereka Panggil 'Drakonian' Untuk Tahan Tanpa Bicara
item.description:
Said by: Lawyers for Liberty / Bar Council / Amnesty International

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Akta Kesalahan Keselamatan (Langkah-Langkah Khas) 2012 (SOSMA), yang membenarkan penahanan tanpa bicara sehingga 28 hari dan menyekat pengawasan kehakiman kes keselamatan, kekal beroperasi sepenuhnya di bawah kerajaan Anwar. PH secara jelas berjanji untuk memansuhkan SOSMA dalam kedua-dua manifesto 2018 dan 2022, memanggilnya ‘drakonian’ dan tidak serasi dengan tadbir urus demokratik.

🔥 Mengapa Ia Penting

Penahanan tanpa bicara secara asasnya tidak serasi dengan kedaulatan undang-undang. SOSMA memberikan kerajaan kuasa untuk menahan individu selama hampir sebulan tanpa tuduhan dan tanpa penelitian kehakiman penuh. Di tangan yang salah, ia alat untuk penganiayaan politik. Setiap hari ia kekal dalam undang-undang ialah hari mana-mana rakyat Malaysia boleh ditahan tanpa perlindungan yang dijanjikan demokrasi.

item.title: [BM] Tuntutan Autonomi Sabah Dan Sarawak Masih Tidak Dipenuhi — Malaysia Timur Kekal Anak Tiri Yang Dilupakan
item.description:
Said by: Sabah & Sarawak Leaders / GPS

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Walaupun pindaan perlembagaan 2021 memulihkan status Sabah dan Sarawak sebagai rakan setara dalam Persekutuan, Malaysia Timur kekal dipinggirkan secara struktur. Sabah adalah negeri termiskin Malaysia. Syor Perjanjian Malaysia 1963 (MA63) berhabuk. Pertikaian royalti minyak dan gas kekal tidak diselesaikan. Perkongsian setara wujud di atas kertas tetapi bukan dalam peruntukan bajet, pelaburan infrastruktur, atau perwakilan politik.

item.title: Brain Drain Accelerating — 1.86 Million Malaysians Have Left, and the Best Keep Leaving
item.description:
Said by: World Bank / Talent Corporation Data

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-01-01

1.86 million Malaysians living abroad, disproportionately highly skilled. Public hospital doctors work 84-hour weeks for poverty wages. 11,000 specialist shortage directly linked to brain drain. Structural causes — race-based policies, low wages, poor governance — remain unaddressed.

item.title: Child Marriage STILL Legal — PH Promised to End It, Then Did Nothing Because 'Islamic Sensitivities'
item.description:
Said by: Sisters in Islam / UNICEF / Women’s Rights Groups

Category: Religion

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

Despite years of campaigning by women’s rights organisations and explicit promises from PH politicians, child marriage remains legal in Malaysia. Under Islamic family law (state jurisdiction), girls as young as 16 can be married with Shariah court approval, and in practice, younger marriages have been documented.

🔥 Why It Matters

Child marriage robs girls of education, economic independence, and bodily autonomy. It is associated with higher rates of domestic violence, poverty, health complications from early pregnancy, and intergenerational disadvantage. UNICEF has repeatedly urged Malaysia to raise the minimum marriage age to 18 for all.

item.title: Civil Servants Get Pensions-for-Life, Private Workers Get Depleting EPF — The Two-Tier Retirement System
item.description:
Said by: Public Finance Analysts / EPF

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-01-01

1.3-1.6M civil servants get defined-benefit pensions for life funded by taxpayers. 16M private sector workers rely on EPF with median balance of RM47,600 that runs out in 5 years. No government has had the courage to reform it because the civil service is a critical vote bank.

item.title: Climate Action Failure — Malaysia's Paris Agreement Pledges Are Fantasy, Emissions Keep Rising
item.description:
Said by: Climate Action Tracker / Environmental Groups

Category: Other

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

Despite being a signatory to the Paris Agreement and making ambitious pledges on carbon emission reductions, Malaysia’s actual emissions trajectory continues upward. Deforestation continues, coal power plants remain operational, data centre energy consumption grows, and the government has offered no credible pathway to meeting its stated climate commitments.

🔥 Why It Matters

Climate change is already affecting Malaysia through more severe floods (2024 devastation), prolonged droughts, rising sea levels threatening coastal communities, and biodiversity loss. The country is simultaneously a victim and contributor — its palm oil industry and deforestation are significant global emission sources. Failure to act on climate isn’t just bad policy — it’s an existential threat to Malaysia’s future.

item.title: Digital Divide Persists — Rural Communities Still Without Reliable Internet While Government Talks 5G
item.description:
Said by: MCMC / Rural Development Ministry

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: As of early 2025, millions of Malaysians in rural Sabah, Sarawak, and the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia still lack reliable internet access. While the government spent billions on the 5G DNB versus Telekom Malaysia dual-network fiasco, the JENDELA programme to improve basic digital infrastructure faced delays and coverage gaps. Students in rural schools were severely disadvantaged during COVID-19 distance learning, and the digital divide has not meaningfully narrowed since. MCMC’s own data shows connectivity gaps between urban and rural areas remain significant, with many rural schools relying on unstable satellite connections or no connectivity at all.

item.title: Gambling Addiction Crisis — 4D, Toto, and Online Betting Destroy Families While Government Collects Revenue
item.description:
Said by: Health Ministry / NGOs

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Malaysia faces a growing gambling addiction crisis driven by legal 4D and Toto outlets, sports betting, and an explosion of illegal online gambling platforms. The government profits from gambling through licensing fees and gaming taxes — collecting billions annually from licensed operators. Meanwhile, gambling addiction destroys lower-income families, with treatment services remaining minimal compared to the scale of the problem. Online gambling has exploded beyond MCMC’s enforcement capacity, with estimates suggesting billions of ringgit flow through illegal platforms annually.

item.title: Gender Pay Gap Persists at 6-9% — Women Do More Work for Less Pay, Government Does Nothing
item.description:
Said by: DOSM / Talentcorp Data

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

Despite Anwar’s government having prominent women in cabinet and occasional rhetoric about gender equality, Malaysia’s gender pay gap remains stubbornly persistent at an estimated 6-9% across sectors, with significantly larger gaps in certain industries. Women bear a disproportionate burden of unpaid care work, face career penalties for motherhood, and are underrepresented in senior management and board positions.

item.title: Higher Education Budget Keeps Shrinking — From 6.8% in 2010 to Just 4.3% in 2025
item.description:
Said by: New Mandala / Academic Analysis

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Malaysia’s higher education budget has dropped from 6.8% of the total national budget in 2010 to just 4.3% in 2025, with the lowest point at 3.9% in 2023. Meanwhile, tertiary enrollment stands at only 42.57% — far below Singapore’s 93% and the global average of 51.98%. Academic analysis describes a “widening disjuncture between reformist discourse and actual financial commitment” to education under PH. While the government talks about the knowledge economy and human capital development, the budget tells a different story.

item.title: Jho Low STILL Free After 8 Years — Malaysia's Most Wanted Fugitive Living Comfortably Somewhere
item.description:
Said by: Interpol / MACC / DOJ

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: As of 2025, Low Taek Jho (Jho Low) — the central figure in the 1MDB scandal — remains free despite Interpol red notices, international arrest warrants, and charges in multiple jurisdictions. Three different Malaysian governments have failed to secure his extradition. Anwar made 1MDB accountability his signature promise, yet has made no visible progress in locating or extraditing Jho Low. Reports suggest he has been residing in China or Macau, but the Malaysian government has not disclosed any diplomatic efforts to secure his return.

item.title: Malaysia Refuses to Ratify ICERD — Anwar Caves to Racial Politics on International Human Rights Treaty
item.description:
Said by: Anwar Ibrahim Administration / Malay-Muslim Groups

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Malaysia remains one of the few countries in the world that has not ratified the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ICERD). In 2018, PH’s attempt to ratify ICERD was abandoned after mass protests led by Malay-Muslim groups who argued it would undermine Bumiputera privileges. Anwar, once a progressive leader committed to equality, has not revisited the issue since becoming PM. The “reformist” Prime Minister has accepted the status quo on racial discrimination — ICERD ratification is not on the agenda.

item.title: Malaysia Tertiary Enrollment at 42.57% — Below Global Average, Far Behind Singapore's 93%
item.description:
Said by: Academic Research / UNESCO Data

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

Only 42.57% of eligible Malaysians enrolled in tertiary education — below global average of 51.98%. Singapore at 93%, US at 88%. Over 10,000 SPM students (2.6%) didn’t even sit for the exam.

item.title: Mental Health Crisis Spiralling — Youth Suicide and Depression Surge While Government Underfunds Services
item.description:
Said by: Health Ministry / WHO Data

Category: Health

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

Malaysia is facing a deepening mental health crisis, particularly among young people, with rising rates of depression, anxiety, and suicide. The National Health and Morbidity Survey has consistently shown alarming increases in mental health issues, with nearly 3 in 10 Malaysians experiencing some form of mental health problem.

🔥 Why It Matters

Youth are disproportionately affected: social media pressure, academic stress, economic uncertainty with 12.28% youth unemployment, and the COVID-19 pandemic’s lingering psychological effects have created a perfect storm. Yet government mental health services remain woefully underfunded and understaffed. Public hospitals face severe shortages of psychiatrists and psychologists, with waiting times stretching weeks or months.

item.title: Palm Oil Deforestation Continues Unchecked — Environmental Pledges vs Plantation Profits
item.description:
Said by: Environmental NGOs / SAM

Category: Other

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Despite Malaysia’s commitments to international climate agreements and sustainable development goals, deforestation for palm oil plantations continues to degrade tropical rainforests among the oldest and most biodiverse on Earth. The Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification scheme has been criticised by international NGOs as inadequate greenwashing. Malaysia’s river water quality is declining — clean rivers dropped from 486 to 468 in 2025. The Perak River turned blue from rare earth mining discharge in November 2025. Endangered species including orangutans, pygmy elephants, and Malayan tigers face shrinking habitats.

item.title: Penang South Islands: $14B Reclamation Project Destroys Fishing Grounds for 6,000 Fishers
item.description:
Said by: Penang State Government / SAM

Category: Other

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: The Penang South Islands (PSI) project — originally three artificial islands costing approximately $14 billion — threatens the livelihoods of 6,000 fishers, 51,184 tonnes of annual marine catch worth RM525 million, and 511 aquaculture farms generating RM1.67 billion per year. After sustained protests from fishing communities and environmental groups including Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM), the project was downsized to one island. However, construction proceeds, and the fundamental impact on fishing grounds and marine ecosystems remains.

item.title: Proton Still Dependent on Government Protections — 40 Years of 'National Car' and Still Can't Compete
item.description:
Said by: Automotive Industry Analysts

Category: Economy

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: After 40 years and billions in public subsidies, tax exemptions, and protectionist trade policies, Proton still cannot compete internationally without government protection. High import duties — excise duties of up to 100% on foreign cars — inflate vehicle prices for 33 million Malaysians. The same car costs half as much in Thailand or Indonesia. Anwar’s government shows no inclination to reform automotive trade policies or phase out protections that cost Malaysian consumers billions annually.

item.title: PTPTN Loan Crisis — Millions Owe Billions, Repayment Rates Abysmal, Graduates Trapped in Debt
item.description:
Said by: PTPTN / Auditor General Reports

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) faces a chronic repayment crisis, with billions of ringgit in outstanding loans and repayment rates that consistently fall short of targets. Millions of Malaysian graduates carry PTPTN debt that limits their ability to save, invest, or purchase homes. The fund’s sustainability is questionable without major reform.

🔥 Why It Matters

PTPTN debt creates a generational poverty trap: graduates enter the workforce already indebted, face an economy with 12.28% youth unemployment, earn wages that barely cover living costs (RM1,500 minimum wage), and must somehow repay student loans while building a life. Many can’t — which is why repayment rates are so low. The cycle feeds itself: unaffordable education → debt → low wages → inability to repay → creditworthiness issues → inability to get mortgages → permanent renter status.

item.title: Road Deaths at Catastrophic Levels — Malaysia Among Deadliest Roads in ASEAN, Government's Response: 'Speed Cameras'
item.description:
Said by: MIROS / WHO Road Safety Data

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Malaysia records over 6,000 road deaths annually — approximately 16 people every day. Motorcyclists make up the largest share of fatalities. WHO data ranks Malaysia among the deadliest roads in ASEAN with a road traffic death rate significantly above the global average. The government’s primary response has been speed cameras, periodic enforcement campaigns, and awareness programmes. No structural reform of road safety infrastructure, licensing standards, or vehicle safety requirements has been implemented under PH.

item.title: Sabah and Sarawak Autonomy Demands Still Unmet — East Malaysia Remains the Forgotten Stepchild
item.description:
Said by: Sabah & Sarawak Leaders / GPS

Category: Politics

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Despite 2021 constitutional amendments restoring Sabah and Sarawak’s status as equal partners in the Federation, East Malaysia remains structurally marginalised. Sabah is Malaysia’s poorest state. MA63 (Malaysia Agreement 1963) recommendations are gathering dust. Oil and gas royalty disputes remain unresolved. Equal partnership exists on paper but not in budget allocation, infrastructure investment, or political representation. Sarawak’s GPS maintains leverage through coalition politics, but Sabah — where PH won only 1 of 20 seats in the 2025 state election — has almost no bargaining power.

item.title: Sedition Act STILL Not Repealed — PH Promised to Abolish It in 2018 and 2022, Then Used It Instead
item.description:
Said by: Lawyers for Liberty / Article 19 / Bar Council

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

The Sedition Act 1948 — a colonial-era law that PH explicitly promised to repeal in both its 2018 and 2022 election manifestos — remains fully operational under the Anwar government. Not only has it not been repealed, it is being actively used against government critics. Activist Chegubard was charged under the Act for his Forest City casino social media post.

item.title: Single Mothers in Poverty — 300,000+ Families Led by Women Living Below the Poverty Line
item.description:
Said by: Women’s Ministry / DOSM Data

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

An estimated 300,000+ single-mother households in Malaysia live at or below the poverty line, facing inadequate government support, employment discrimination, and insufficient childcare infrastructure. Single mothers are disproportionately represented among B40 households and face barriers including limited access to affordable housing, healthcare, and skills training.

🔥 Why It Matters

Single mothers and their children represent one of the most vulnerable demographics in Malaysia. Children in these households face higher risks of educational dropout, malnutrition, and intergenerational poverty. The lack of affordable childcare forces many single mothers to choose between working (and leaving children unsupervised) or staying home (and being unable to afford basic needs).

item.title: SOSMA Still Unrepealed — PH Using the Security Law They Called 'Draconian' to Detain Without Trial
item.description:
Said by: Lawyers for Liberty / Bar Council / Amnesty International

Category: Social

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 What Happened

The Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (SOSMA), which allows detention without trial for up to 28 days and restricts judicial oversight of security cases, remains fully operational under the Anwar government. PH explicitly promised to repeal SOSMA in both its 2018 and 2022 manifestos, calling it ‘draconian’ and incompatible with democratic governance.

item.title: Teacher Shortage in Rural Schools — Kids in Kampungs Get Second-Class Education
item.description:
Said by: Education Ministry / NUTP

Category: Education

Date: 2025-01-01

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: Rural schools across Malaysia face chronic teacher shortages in mathematics, science, and English — the three subjects most critical for economic competitiveness. Indigenous communities in Sabah, Sarawak, and Orang Asli settlements face the worst gaps, with some schools lacking qualified teachers entirely for key subjects. The National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP) has repeatedly raised the issue. The Education Ministry acknowledges the shortage but has not implemented structural reforms to address it.

item.title: [BM] MCA Kepada PH: 'Jangan Salahkan BN Untuk Kegagalan ANDA Mereformasi'
item.description:
Said by: Neow Choo Seong, MCA Youth

Category: Politics

Date: 2024-12-30

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Pada akhir Disember 2024, jurucakap Pemuda MCA Neow Choo Seong mengeluarkan kenyataan memberitahu PH supaya berhenti menyalahkan BN atas kegagalan PH melaksanakan reformasi yang dijanjikan. Neow berhujah bahawa “kuasa berada sepenuhnya di tangan PH” dan BN tidak patut dijadikan kambing hitam atas keengganan PH sendiri bertindak. Kenyataan ini ketara kerana MCA adalah parti komponen BN dalam gabungan kerajaan perpaduan — bermakna rakan gabungan PH sendiri sudah jemu PH menyalahkan semua orang lain atas kegagalannya menyampaikan reformasi.

item.title: MCA to PH: 'Don't Blame BN for YOUR Failure to Reform'
item.description:
Said by: Neow Choo Seong, MCA Youth

Category: Politics

Date: 2024-12-30

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: In late December 2024, MCA Youth spokesman Neow Choo Seong issued a statement telling PH to stop blaming BN for PH’s failure to implement promised reforms. Neow argued that “power is firmly in PH’s hands” and BN should not be scapegoated for PH’s own inaction. The statement was notable because MCA is a BN component party within the unity government coalition — meaning even PH’s own coalition partners were tired of PH blaming everyone else for its failure to deliver reform.

item.title: [BM] Akta Keselamatan Dalam Talian Diluluskan — SKMM Dapat Kuasa Penapisan Menyeluruh, Tiada Pengawasan
item.description:
Said by: Parliament / Fahmi Fadzil

Category: Social

Date: 2024-12-20

📌 APA YANG BERLAKU: Pada Disember 2024, Parlimen meluluskan Akta Keselamatan Dalam Talian dan pindaan AKM yang memberi SKMM kuasa penapisan menyeluruh dengan penalti sehingga RM10 juta bagi platform yang tidak patuh. Perundangan ini memberi kuasa kepada SKMM untuk mengarahkan penyingkiran kandungan, menyekat laman web dan menghukum syarikat media sosial — semuanya tanpa pengawasan kehakiman bebas. Menteri Komunikasi Fahmi Fadzil menggambarkannya sebagai perlu untuk melindungi kanak-kanak dan membanteras ancaman siber. Freedom House membenderakannya sebagai kemunduran besar dalam kebebasan internet. Tiada mekanisme pengawasan bebas dimasukkan.

item.title: Online Safety Act Passes — MCMC Gets Sweeping Censorship Powers, No Oversight
item.description:
Said by: Parliament / Fahmi Fadzil

Category: Social

Date: 2024-12-20

📌 WHAT HAPPENED: In December 2024, Parliament passed the Online Safety Act and CMA amendments giving MCMC sweeping censorship powers with penalties up to RM10 million for non-compliant platforms. The legislation empowers MCMC to order content removal, block websites, and penalise social media companies — all without independent judicial oversight. Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil described it as necessary to protect children and combat cyber threats. Freedom House flagged it as a major regression in internet freedom. No independent oversight mechanism was included.

item.title: [BM] Rosmah Dibebaskan Dari Semua 17 Tuduhan Pengubahan Wang Haram — Ahli Politik PH Yang Serang Beliau Sedekad Tiba-Tiba Bisu
item.description:
Said by: PH Politicians (Tony Pua, Rafizi Ramli, et al.) / High Court

Category: Politics

Date: 2024-12-19

📌 Apa Yang Berlaku

Pada 19 Disember 2024, Hakim Mahkamah Tinggi K. Muniandy membebaskan Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor — isteri bekas PM Najib Razak yang dipenjara — daripada kesemua 17 tuduhan dalam kes pengubahan wang haram dan pengelakan cukai melibatkan RM7.09 juta. Hakim memutuskan pihak pendakwaan gagal mengemukakan elemen utama kesalahan. Rosmah didakwa pada Oktober 2018 dengan 12 tuduhan pengubahan wang haram dan 5 tuduhan gagal mengisytiharkan pendapatan.
